summary: The verifier compares every statement field type-strictly against expectations from an independent manual model. Each named TD-7 rule has a sealed family whose outcome changes when that rule is wrong. The two manual-unreached steps (sub-2,000-cent corrections and sub-1,000-cent partial weeks) are pinned by edge-placed sealed cases and shipped-package differentials. Contract-valid key order and wage-line order are accepted. No defect with a wrong grading outcome was found.

unread_or_truncated_ranges: tests/shipped/app/** not opened separately: the manifest gives identical SHA-256 hashes to the environment/app files that were read

checks_performed: Mapped each manual rule (2.2-2.8, 3.1-3.5, 4.1-4.3, 5.1-5.2, 6.1) to its test in tests/test_outputs.py and to the shipped defect it must catch: week-of-payday crediting, the weeks-paid divisor, the 3/5 rate, the newest row, 7 waiting days, period days without +1, the floored TTD, and 3/5 partial benefits for every week

Checked tests/manual_model.py step by step against the manual: AWW rounded after dividing by 13, rate taken from the rounded AWW, 3.5 applied before the clamp, nearest-cent TTD and partial rounding, and a partial cap equal to the rate. Also checked that the divisors 13, 3, 5 and 7 never produce an exact half-cent

Hand-verified the correction edge cases in corrections.jsonl and differential-corrections.jsonl on both base-period edges (a payday in the week of injury, and a payday in the oldest base week). A move-back-one-week implementation of corrections changes AWW there and fails

Hand-verified that in the differential-low_partial_weeks jobs the shipped AWW and rate equal the manual values (13 weeks paid, and the rate clamped to the same max or min). Rows 3-4 give 3/5 shares below the rate, so a 2/3 share or a zero benefit for low weeks is rejected. In low_partial_weeks.jsonl W533089 and W543087 check 3/5 against 2/3
Checked the comparator: exact top-level key, statement count and order, key set compared as a set (any key order accepted), and type(x) is int, which rejects floats and booleans

Checked that the relabel and drawn-job paths keep expectations consistent (wage lines shuffled, which the README allows; claims reordered with matching expected order) and that drawn jobs stay within section 1 and avoid both manual-unreached inputs

Checked the driver byte-equality requirement against the instruction, and checked candidate execution (python3 -I -S as uid 65534, fresh cwd, /app sealed) for false-rejection risk to contract-valid stdlib solutions

coverage_sweep.category: Map each required behavior to an assertion that fails if missing or reversed
coverage_sweep.reason: Each manual rule has a named test with a sealed family, and each family was read. Each shipped defect changes at least one compared field in its family, for example waiting_days 7 vs 3, period days without +1, the 3/5 vs 2/3 rate, the newest row vs the row in force on the injury date, AWW divided by weeks paid vs 13, and floor vs nearest TTD

coverage_sweep.category: Check the full core result, not existence, keys or row count
coverage_sweep.reason: compare() checks every one of the ten fields for exact value and exact type in every statement, in job order

coverage_sweep.category: Each named domain rule has a case whose outcome changes when the rule is wrong
coverage_sweep.reason: The 2,000-cent week's-pay threshold (weeks_pay_threshold, 2000 vs 1999), the 1,000-cent partial threshold (partial_week_threshold, with 3/5 on 999 cents in low_partial_weeks), 13 vs 14 disability days in one and in three periods (retroactive_days), the day before/on/after a row change (row_in_force), 3.5 below the minimum (low_wage_rate, and rows 1-3 of limits_job), the rate cap on partial benefits (partial_benefit W661070/W375072) and the zero-loss week (no_wage_loss) each have a discriminating case

The shipped package, a partial fix (for example 2/3 of a low week, a zero benefit for low weeks, or corrections moved back a week), a divisor counting only weeks paid, and a rate row taken from the disability start each change a compared value in a sealed family or in the drawn-job model comparison. Figures drawn fresh at run time defeat an embedded answer table

Statement key order is compared as a set. JSON whitespace is irrelevant because output is parsed. Wage-line order is shuffled, as the README says it is 'in no particular order'. Claim numbers with spaces, quotes, backslashes and non-ASCII characters are compared as strings. No exact-half rounding case exists, so the rounding direction is never at issue. Running with -I -S does not affect a stdlib-only package in /app/src

coverage_sweep.category: Documented restrictions and lifecycle behavior are enforced
coverage_sweep.reason: The instruction requires the driver to be left byte-identical. test_submitted_driver_unchanged and test.sh cmp enforce this, and jobs run through the verifier's own driver against the candidate's /app/src, as the instruction states. 'Add no exception, clamp or guard' is backed where it can change output: an added clamp on the low-wage rate or on low-week benefits changes the low_wage_rate and differential expectations

coverage_sweep.category: Initialization and first-event transitions, and signed derived quantities
coverage_sweep.reason: The waiting period starts from the first disability day of the claim, not of each period; the three-period cases in waiting_period and retroactive_days discriminate a per-period reading. Wage loss is non-negative by 2.7 and is tested on both sides (at, below and above AWW in no_wage_loss; earnings above AWW in limits_claims)

coverage_sweep.category: Manual-unreached steps kept at today's code (instruction paragraph 2)
coverage_sweep.reason: The model's 'Shipped step' branches (corrections credited to their payday's week; low weeks at 3/5 of the manual wage loss, capped at the manual rate) follow the instruction's rule that inputs the manual settles take manual values. The differentials compare with the real shipped package only where the manual and shipped AWW and rate coincide, which was verified by hand

coverage_sweep.category: Stale binaries, proxy behavior, and self-controlled comparisons
coverage_sweep.reason: Expectations come from sealed files pinned by ROSTER digests, from hand-worked statements and from the verifier's own model. Candidate output is never used as its own reference. The verifier's driver copy is installed before candidate code runs

rules: 2.2/3.1 week's pay shifts back a week
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: The same payday carries a week's pay and a sub-2,000 correction at each base-period edge (W854080 on 2018-09-14; W595082 on 2019-03-22). The week's pay moves into the base period while the correction stays outside, or the reverse
In W884039 (AWW 44,999 < min 45,000) the rate is 44,999 and partial benefits are capped at that rate, not at the row minimum
W345021 has no wages, so AWW 0 < min gives rate 0 and TTD 0, and partial weeks give tpd 0. The shipped code would divide by zero here
W784054 has 14 days over three periods and gets retro 3. W335052 has 13 days in one period and gets retro 0
row_in_force jobs place the injury the day before, on and after a row change, with high-wage (max-bound) and low-wage (3.5 or min-bound) claims
999 cents takes the 3/5 share and 1,000 cents takes the 2/3 share (W543087, W533089, partial_week_threshold)
